subtype: Insults, taunts and challenges among peers [Interpreting]
passage: Noor, when I was fifteen, and yes, this is your Hafsa khala talking, a boy named Pran said, in front of the whole bus, "Nice haircut, did you lose a bet?" Everyone laughed. I didn't know if he was joking, because he said it with a grin and we had teased each other for years. I looked at my friends. They were laughing at him too, so I laughed and said, "Yes, I lost to a goat." That was banter. But a month later a boy from another school sent nasty messages in a group chat and dared me to answer, again and again. That felt like an attack meant to provoke. I did not answer. I took screenshots and showed my mother, and the messages stopped.

qa.q: Where did Pran make the remark about the haircut?
qa.a: He made it on the bus, in front of everyone.

qa.q: Why did Hafsa feel the messages from the boy from another school were different?
qa.a: They were nasty, repeated and came with dares to answer, so she felt wary and treated them as an attack meant to provoke. Pran's remark came with a grin from someone she had teased for years.

qa.q: What protective steps did Hafsa take?
qa.a: She did not answer, saved screenshots and showed her mother.

qa.q: How might Pran have seen his joke on the bus?
qa.a: Probably as ordinary teasing between friends, though it may not have felt the same to everyone listening.

grounding: An elder tells how tone, history and audience separate banter from attack, and not answering and saving evidence protect.

subtype: Insults, taunts and challenges among peers [Interpreting]
passage: The bus was loud and the match on the driver's radio drowned out most of it. Bhavna's phone buzzed. In the class group, a boy had posted, 'Bet you can't score even one goal, Bhavna. Dare you to try in front of everyone.' A few laughing emojis followed. Minakshi, sitting next to her, leaned over. "Is this a joke or a shove?" Bhavna's cheeks burned. She looked at who sent it, remembered he had done this before, and noticed the crowd of watchers. "It's not friendly." She did not type a reply. Instead she took a screenshot and whispered, "Can you help me show this to Ma'am tomorrow?" Minakshi nodded and squeezed her hand.

qa.q: Whose phone buzzed on the bus?
What made Bhavna decide the message was not friendly?
qa.a: She looked at who sent it, remembered he had done this before and noticed the crowd watching, so it felt like a shove meant to provoke her. Her burning cheeks show it hurt.

qa.q: What steps did Bhavna take that protect her?
qa.a: She did not reply, she took a screenshot and asked Minakshi to help show it to Ma'am.

qa.q: How might the boy who posted it see the message?
qa.a: He may say he was only joking, but the past pattern and the audience suggest it was meant to provoke.

grounding: A teen reads tone, history and audience to see an online taunt as an attack, and does not reply but saves evidence.
